headline: A stopgap spending law that keeps the government funded through December 20, 2019, extends many expiring programs, and gives military members a 3.1% pay raise.
what_it_does: The law provides temporary federal funding for FY2020 so agencies can keep operating and a shutdown is avoided while full spending bills are still pending. It mostly keeps funding at FY2019 levels, with some exceptions such as extra money for the 2020 Census, Indian Health Service, and Ebola response. It also extends many programs that were set to expire, including community health centers, the Special Diabetes Programs, TANF grants, and the National Flood Insurance Program. It additionally repeals a provision that would have permanently rescinded $7.569 billion in state highway funding and allows a third round of payments from the Victims of State Sponsored Terrorism Fund.

who_it_affects.how: They receive a 3.1% pay raise under the law.

who_it_affects.group: Patients at community health centers and people in the National Health Service Corps
who_it_affects.how: The enhanced funding for these centers and the Corps is extended.

who_it_affects.group: People with diabetes, including American Indians served by the Indian Health Service
who_it_affects.how: The Special Diabetes Program and the Special Diabetes Program for Indians are extended.

who_it_affects.group: Low-income families receiving Temporary Assistance for Needy Families grants
who_it_affects.how: TANF grants to states and related assistance to U.S. territories continue under an extension.
A scheduled permanent cut of $7.569 billion in FY2020 federal highway funding is repealed.

who_it_affects.group: Federal employees and agencies that rely on annual appropriations
who_it_affects.how: They keep operating at FY2019 funding levels through December 20, 2019, instead of facing a shutdown.

who_it_affects.group: Families of 9/11 victims and certain Iran hostage crisis victims
who_it_affects.how: They may be eligible for payments from the Victims of State Sponsored Terrorism Fund under the new categories.

who_it_affects.group: Homeowners and communities in flood-prone areas
who_it_affects.how: Coverage under the National Flood Insurance Program is extended through December 20, 2019.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted November 21, 2019; the funding and extensions generally run through December 20, 2019, though some provisions have different timelines.
